name: Nurse Job Interview (US / UK / Australia)
description: Evaluates an internationally educated nurse answering a hospital, recruiter, or staffing-agency interview in English: structured behavioural answers, clinical-scenario answers within nursing scope, and motivation for working abroad.

anchors.80-100: Answers flow naturally at a steady pace; pauses sound like thinking, not word-searching.
anchors.50-70: Understandable, with hesitations or restarts that interrupt longer answers.
anchors.10-40: Frequent breakdowns; the interviewer has to prompt to get a complete answer.

anchors.80-100: Accurate past-tense narration and professional nursing vocabulary; errors are rare and minor.
anchors.50-70: Mostly accurate; tense or article errors are noticeable but meaning is clear.
anchors.10-40: Errors regularly obscure what the candidate did or would do.

anchors.80-100: Behavioural answers name a specific Situation and Task, spend most of the time on the candidate's own Actions, and end with a Result and what they learned.
anchors.50-70: A real example, but the actions are vague ('we did') or the result is missing.
anchors.10-40: Hypothetical or generic answers ('I always...') where a specific example was asked for.

anchors.80-100: Clinical-scenario answers prioritise safety (assess, intervene within scope, escalate, document) in a clear order, using the ABC/prioritisation logic an employer expects.
anchors.50-70: Safe overall but the order of priorities is unclear, or escalation is left implicit.
anchors.10-40: Unsafe, out of scope, or no escalation for a deteriorating patient.

anchors.80-100: Specific, credible reasons for this role and country; confident without overclaiming; asks a thoughtful question when invited.
anchors.50-70: Positive but generic motivation; modest to the point of underselling real experience.
anchors.10-40: No clear motivation, negative about previous employers, or unprofessional.

anchors.80-100: Clinical details mentioned in answers are accurate and use the target country's terminology.
anchors.50-70: Mostly accurate; some home-country terms or abbreviations left unexplained.
anchors.10-40: Clinical statements are inaccurate in ways an employer would notice.

checklist.item: Opened with a concise professional introduction (current role, experience, specialty)
Answered at least one behavioural question with a specific example in Situation-Task-Action-Result order
Described their own actions in the first person rather than 'we'
Gave a clinical-scenario answer that assessed, acted within scope, and escalated
Gave specific, credible motivation for this role and country
Asked the interviewer a relevant question when invited
